text: Spline interpolation Splines join piecewise low-degree polynomials with specified continuity. Distinguish them from a single global high-degree polynomial and distinguish exact interpolation from smoothing noisy data. Problem and representative equations Use a nondecreasing knot sequence tᵢ and degree p. Nᵢ,₀ is the indicator of [tᵢ,tᵢ₊₁); zero-denominator terms in the recursion are defined as zero. Degree p means order p+1. Ni,p(x)=x−titi+p−tiNi,p−1(x)+ti+p+1−xti+p+1−ti+1Ni+1,p−1(x),s(x)=∑iciNi,p(x).Ni,p​(x)=ti+p​−ti​x−ti​​Ni,p−1​(x)+ti+p+1​−ti+1​ti+p+1​−x​Ni+1,p−1​(x),s(x)=i∑​ci​Ni,p​(x). Algorithm Represent s=ΣcᵢNᵢ,ₚ and determine coefficients by interpolation or least squares. A natural cubic spline sets endpoint second derivatives to zero; clamped conditions prescribe endpoint first derivatives. Determining coefficients and evaluating the spline by de Boor’s algorithm are separate stages. Conditions and pitfalls An interior knot of multiplicity r generally gives Cᵖ⁻ʳ continuity. Cubic splines do not automatically preserve monotonicity or positivity and can overshoot. Extrapolation depends on the chosen endpoint convention and is not covered by an in-interval interpolation argument. What to check Check polynomial reproduction, one-sided derivatives at knots and endpoint conditions. For noiseless functions study refinement; for noisy data separately report held-out prediction errors and smoothing-parameter dependence.
